title: Assistant Manager (01464) - 3830 Ruckriegal Pkwy Suite 101
description:
We're looking for an enthusiastic and detail-oriented Assistant Manager to join our team at our Jeffersontown location (3830 Ruckriegal Pkwy Suite 101). In this role, you'll play a key part in driving operational excellence and creating a positive, customer-focused environment. As Assistant Manager, you'll support the management team in overseeing daily store operations while fostering a collaborative and motivated workplace where both team members and customers thrive.

  • Oversee daily store operations, ensuring efficient workflows and consistent delivery of excellent customer service
  • Lead, motivate, and support team members to maintain a positive and productive work environment
  • Run shifts effectively, making decisive, real-time decisions to optimize performance and address challenges
  • Manage financial transactions with accuracy and maintain proper cash handling procedures
  • Engage with customers professionally and empathetically, addressing concerns and ensuring satisfaction
  • Assist in implementing and communicating company policies, procedures, and standards across the team
  • Maintain a clean, organized, and well-stocked store environment that reflects company standards
  • Collaborate with the management team to establish and achieve store goals and drive continuous improvement
  • Participate in employee training, development, and onboarding initiatives to build a skilled team
  • Ensure compliance with food safety regulations and quality standards, conducting regular audits and reviews
  • Manage inventory levels and coordinate stock ordering to maintain optimal supply levels
  • Analyze performance metrics and provide feedback to support team development and accountability
  • Resolve conflicts and handle challenging situations with professionalism and transparency
  • Proven experience in retail or food service management, with a demonstrated track record of successfully running shifts and leading operations
  • Strong leadership skills with the ability to motivate, develop, and manage a diverse team effectively
  • Excellent customer service skills with a friendly, approachable demeanor and genuine commitment to customer satisfaction
  • Solid mathematical aptitude and demonstrated money management abilities, including cash handling and financial accuracy
  • Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to make quick, informed decisions in fast-paced environments
  • Proficiency in multitasking and prioritizing multiple responsibilities simultaneously
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills with the ability to convey information clearly to diverse audiences
  • Detail-oriented mindset with a focus on maintaining high standards of cleanliness, organization, and quality
  • Comprehensive knowledge of food safety regulations and a commitment to maintaining compliance and quality standards
  • Flexibility to work various shifts, including evenings, weekends, and holidays as needed
  • Physical ability to lift up to 25 pounds regularly and stand for extended periods
  • Proficiency with point-of-sale (POS) systems and basic computer skills
  • Experience with inventory management and stock coordination
  • Ability to analyze performance data and use insights to drive improvements
  • Strong interpersonal and conflict resolution skills
  • High school diploma or equivalent (preferred)

What are we looking for?

The good news is we can teach you how to answer the phone and make a perfect pizza. But here are a few skills you should have to be a successful Assistant Manager:
•Experience leading a team; during your shift, you will manage a staff of anywhere from 3 to 15 people. You will need to use your stellar attitude and motivational skills to get them in the right place, at the right time and doing the right thing all while creating a great place to work.
•A clean driving record and the ability to pass a Motor Vehicle Record check. Safety is a priority for us and we want to make sure anyone we put on the road is safe to be there. You will also need access to reliable vehicle that is insured and have a valid driver's license
•A great role model - you're the person everyone will look to. From being on time for your shift, to having a great attitude to customers and co-workers and even how you dress - you have to have high standards for yourself and the rest of the team.
•Our stores are open 365 days a week. Yes, that's right even on the weekends and the holidays; that's when we are busiest! While you schedule is pretty flexible, you have to be willing to work when the team needs you the most.
•You have to be at least 18 years old.
You'll be working for a company that is fun and flexible. Not to mention, its work experience you will rely on for a long time to come. You've had our pizza delivered to you, now it's time to help up be the pizza delivery company in the world. Go on, boss, show us what you've got. Apply now!

title: Director, Board Relations and Special Projects
description:
Position Title: Director, Board Relations and Special Projects

Department: President’s Office

Reports to: President

FLSA Status: Full-time Exempt, Non-Union

Grade: 4

Position Description:

The Director, Board Relations and Special Projects provides strategic leadership and institutional project management in the Executive Office. Partnering with the President/CEO and Chief Development Officer, the Director is responsible for the management of BBG’s relationship with the Board, including governance and compliance, recruitment, prioritization, communications, and stewardship. This role also oversees institution-wide projects, including tracking and reporting on the implementation of the strategic plan and other cross-departmental projects such as all-staff meetings, retreats, and other major institutional undertakings.


Responsibilities:

Board of Trustees Strategic Program Management

  • In collaboration with the senior leadership team, establish, maintain, and adjust strategy, content, and schedules for annual Board meetings and committee meetings.
  • Working with the President/CEO, key Board Committee Chairs, and appropriate senior staff, develop governing documents and cohesive annual plans and goals for the various Board Committees.
  • Support governance processes and compliance, regularly monitoring bylaws, keeping election cycles, and supporting the creation and revision of policies as needed.
  • Lead process for deliverables and materials including board reports, presentation decks, agendas, meeting minutes, speaker remarks, and other related collateral.
  • Attend all committee meetings, acting as a key link among the Board, President/CEO, and senior leadership team so that information flows clearly and expectations stay aligned.
  • Work closely and proactively with the President/CEO and senior staff to keep staff leadership informed of and prepared for upcoming board-related commitments and responsibilities, and to ensure appropriate follow-up actions and communications.

Board Recruitment, Development, Stewardship, and Communications

  • Partner actively with the Chair of the Nominations and Governance Committee, President/CEO, and CDO to manage a pipeline for Board recruitment, monitoring key attributes, skill sets, and demographics to ensure a diverse and skilled Board serving the needs and ambitions of the institution.
  • Develop and implement processes for Board Recruitment, Orientation, and Development.
  • Plan and execute regular Board retreats, developing timely content and topical materials; plan and execute Board volunteer days in conjunction with Development event staff.
  • Maintain data on Board composition and demographics for DCLA and funders as well as for internal use.
  • Maintain file-sharing repository for onboarding items, as well as ongoing Board development materials, Board meeting materials, and communications toolkits.
  • Develop and execute the President/CEO’s Board communications and engagement strategy, ensuring a year-round information flow, communications, and activities and an engaged, informed, and thriving Board.
  • Working with President/CEO and CDO, plan and execute an appropriate donor stewardship/donor engagement and recognition program for all Board members.

Office of the President/CEO Special Projects

  • Serve as a main project-execution partner to the President/CEO.
  • Prepare briefing materials for the President/CEO in preparation for meetings, conferences, and travel (including assisting with the drafting decks and presentation materials), working closely with Development and program staff.
  • Project-manage reporting and execution of the Strategic Plan and other short- and long-term projects as selected by the President/CEO.
  • Support all-staff and cross-department functions, such as preparation of materials for all-staff and Directors’ meetings, planning of content for the annual staff retreat, and ensuring timely discussion of major institutional topics.
  • Partner with the President/CEO to ensure efficient use of the Senior Leadership Team meeting.


Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent prior work experience in nonprofit settings required
  • 3–5 years of executive-level board relations required
  • Prior administrative and project management experience required
  • Proven ability to work independently and manage multiple projects and activities simultaneously
  • Ability to maintain confidentiality of records and information, diplomacy, tact, and professionalism in actions and appearance
  • Strong administrative and project management skills, including familiarity with project management and constituent relations tools
  • Proactive, consistent, and clear business communication skills, including timely follow up and follow through on projects and tasks
  • Demonstrated written communication skills including advanced proficiency in creating PowerPoint presentations
  • High degree of proficiency with typical office technology, including Microsoft Office applications or Google Suite equivalents and project management platforms, and ability to learn new software platforms quickly
  • Willingness to learn about BBG
  • Strong attention to detail, with a commitment to high-quality work


Compensation and Benefits:

  • Salary Range: $120K–$140K

Brooklyn Botanic Garden considers several factors when determining the appropriate salary to offer a candidate within the listed salary range. title: Program Coordinator II
description:
Overview

The Program Coordinator II supports the statewide implementation, coordination, evaluation, and continuous quality improvement of the Utah Pyramid Model (UPM), a comprehensive, evidence-based framework designed to promote the social and emotional development of young children from birth through age five.

The Utah Pyramid Model is a statewide initiative that supports early care and education professionals, early intervention providers, families, and community partners in implementing evidence-based practices that promote positive social and emotional development, prevent and reduce challenging behaviors, and provide individualized intensive interventions for children with persistent challenging behaviors and their families.

This position provides statewide leadership and coordination in the areas of professional development, training and technical assistance, implementation science, data management, program evaluation, and sustainability. The Program Coordinator II works collaboratively with implementation sites, external and internal coaches, the UPM team, the State Leadership Team, and state and community partners to build the capacity of early childhood systems to implement the Pyramid Model with fidelity.

The position is responsible for supporting the development and delivery of a coordinated statewide system of personnel development, monitoring implementation progress, analyzing program outcomes, and using data to inform decisions at the program and state levels. The Program Coordinator II also contributes to grant development, resource acquisition, and strategic planning to support the continued growth and sustainability of the Utah Pyramid Model.

This position is eligible for telework in the state of Utah.

Exempt positions are eligible for excellent benefits including: 13 paid holidays, earn 22 days of paid vacation leave and 12 days of sick leave per year, 50% tuition reduction for employees and dependents, competitive health benefits packages and a generous contribution into your retirement. View more information here: Summary of Benefits 2026-2027.

Responsibilities

  • Statewide Program Coordination and Implementation
    • Support the statewide coordination, development, and implementation of the Utah Pyramid Model across early care and education and early intervention settings.
    • Coordinate with implementation sites to support consistent application of Pyramid Model practices and alignment with statewide implementation expectations.
    • Apply Implementation Science frameworks and principles to guide the adoption, implementation, and sustainability of evidence-based practices.
    • Support implementation sites as they progress through established stages of Pyramid Model implementation.
    • Collaborate with the UPM team, external coaches, internal coaches, and site leadership teams to identify implementation needs, establish priorities, and address barriers to implementation.
    • Support the development, refinement, and delivery of statewide professional development and technical assistance systems.
    • Participate in statewide partnerships and initiatives that strengthen early childhood systems and expand access to evidence-based social and emotional supports.
  • Pyramid Model Implementation Data System (PIDS)
    • Coordinate and guide the development and delivery of training and technical assistance related to the Pyramid Model Implementation Data System (PIDS).
    • Collaborate with the UPM team to ensure implementation sites, external coaches, internal coaches, and data collectors have the knowledge and resources necessary to use PIDS effectively.
    • Develop and deliver training addressing:
      • Accurate and complete data entry.
      • Navigation and functionality of the PIDS database.
      • Data reporting and interpretation.
      • Use of data to inform implementation decisions and monitor fidelity.
    • Provide ongoing, periodic, and individualized technical assistance based on implementation site needs and readiness.
    • Monitor the PIDS database to support accurate, complete, and timely data entry.
    • Review data for completeness, consistency, and alignment with required data fields.
    • Identify data quality concerns and collaborate with site personnel to resolve discrepancies and improve data collection practices.
    • Communicate with implementation sites and coaches regarding reporting expectations, submission timelines, and data entry requirements.
    • Generate periodic reports to monitor data submission, identify trends, and determine areas requiring follow-up.
    • Support implementation sites in using PIDS data to guide program-wide implementation and continuous quality improvement.
    • Participate in PIDS Community of Practice activities and communicate relevant updates, system developments, contracting information, and recommendations to UPM leadership.
  • Data-Informed Decision-Making and Continuous Quality Improvement
    • Collect, organize, analyze, and interpret program data to monitor statewide implementation progress and outcomes.
    • Develop and maintain reporting systems and program records to meet state, federal, grant, and program reporting requirements.
    • Guide the use of the Look-Think-Act process to support data-informed decision-making among implementation sites, the UPM team, and the State Leadership Team.
    • Promote the systematic use of Pyramid Model implementation and fidelity tools, including:
      • Pyramid Model fidelity observation tools (TPOT and TPITOS).
      • Pyramid Model Benchmark of Quality (BoQ).
      • UPM Strengths and Needs Assessment.
      • Practitioner and Leadership Coaching Logs.
      • Behavior Incident Reporting System (BIRS) social and emotional screening tools.
    • Support implementation sites in interpreting data, identifying strengths and needs, developing action plans, and monitoring progress toward implementation goals.
    • Identify statewide trends and areas of need to inform professional development, coaching, technical assistance, and resource allocation.
    • Collaborate with the State Leadership Team to use data for strategic planning and statewide continuous quality improvement.
  • Statewide Program Outcome Evaluation
    • Collaborate with the UPM team and stakeholders on the development and implementation of evaluation strategies to assess the effectiveness and impact of the Utah Pyramid Model.
    • Collaborate with the UPM team and stakeholders to establish evaluation priorities, measurable outcomes, and methods for assessing statewide implementation.
    • Evaluate outcomes related to:
      • Child social and emotional development and behavior.
      • Program-level implementation and organizational capacity.
      • Family engagement and family outcomes.
      • Implementation fidelity and progress across implementation stages.
      • Training effectiveness and participant satisfaction.
      • Coaching effectiveness and professional development outcomes.
      • Additional priorities identified through needs assessments and stakeholder input.
    • Integrate and analyze multiple sources of program data, including:
      • Pyramid Model Implementation Data System (PIDS).
      • Training evaluations and participant feedback surveys.
      • Teacher and practitioner surveys.
      • Family surveys
      • State Leadership Team evaluation questions and feedback.
      • Fidelity assessments and implementation measures.
    • Develop evaluation reports, summaries, and presentations to communicate program outcomes, implementation progress, and areas for improvement.
    • Ensure evaluation findings are used to guide statewide strategic planning, professional development, coaching supports, resource allocation, and continuous quality improvement.
    • Support implementation sites, the UPM team, and the State Leadership Team in applying the Look-Think-Act process to interpret evaluation findings and determine appropriate next steps.
    • Monitor progress toward statewide program goals and provide information to support grant reporting, funding requirements, and program sustainability.
  • External Coaching and Implementation Support
    • Serve as an External Coach to assigned Pyramid Model implementation sites, providing ongoing training, technical assistance, and implementation support.
    • Support implementation sites in adopting and sustaining Pyramid Model practices with fidelity.
    • Facilitate Pyramid Model training for implementation site teams, ensuring content aligns with statewide standards and addresses site-specific needs.
    • Provide guidance to Program Leadership Teams (PLTs) in developing and maintaining the organizational structures necessary for successful implementation.
    • Support Program Leadership Teams in completing the Benchmark of Quality (BoQ) twice annually, including:
      • Facilitating the BoQ self-assessment process.
      • Assisting teams in identifying strengths and areas for improvement.
      • Supporting the development and refinement of implementation action plans.
      • Monitoring progress toward identified goals and fidelity benchmarks.
    • Provide individualized coaching and technical assistance to support implementation progress and address barriers.
    • Collaborate with internal coaches and site leadership to strengthen coaching systems and promote sustainability.
    • Document coaching activities, implementation progress, and technical assistance using established program documentation systems.
  • Grant Development and Funding Sustainability
    • Participate in grant development and writing activities to support the continued funding and sustainability of the Utah Pyramid Model.
    • Contribute to grant proposals focused on expanding or enhancing Pyramid Model initiatives, including statewide professional development, training and technical assistance, coaching, implementation supports, and program evaluation.
    • Identify funding opportunities that align with UPM priorities and support the continued development of statewide early childhood systems.
    • Collaborate with UPM leadership and institutional partners to develop proposals, establish program objectives, prepare evaluation plans, and identify measurable outcomes.
    • Contribute to additional grant-writing efforts that support the sustainability of the position and broader initiatives within the Institute for Disability Research, Policy & Practice (IDRPP), including projects that extend beyond the scope of the Utah Pyramid Model.
  • Statewide Collaboration and Professional Leadership
    • Participate in and contribute to the work of the UPM State Leadership Team and other statewide early childhood initiatives.
    • Establish and maintain collaborative relationships with state agencies, early intervention programs, school districts, early care and education providers, Head Start programs, and community partners.
    • Participate in statewide professional learning communities, communities of practice, and collaborative initiatives that strengthen Pyramid Model implementation.
    • Share program outcomes, evaluation findings, implementation updates, and recommendations with UPM leadership and stakeholders.
    • Represent the Utah Pyramid Model in relevant statewide and regional meetings, professional development opportunities, and conferences.
    • Contribute to the development of resources, training materials, and professional learning opportunities that strengthen the capacity of the early childhood workforce.
  • Additional Responsibilities
    • Perform other program-related duties as assigned that support the goals and priorities of the Utah Pyramid Model, IDRPP, and affiliated initiatives.
    • Contribute to special projects, program development activities, and emerging initiatives as needed.
    • Demonstrate flexibility, responsiveness, and collaborative problem-solving in addressing program needs and institutional priorities.

Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in a related field plus two years of relevant work experience; or a master's degree in a related field; or an equivalent combination of education plus experience is required.
  • Experience in early care and education or early intervention settings, working with children birth through age five and their families.
  • Experience with program coordination, program implementation, or the development and delivery of professional development and technical assistance.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Master's degree in a related field and relevant professional experience in early care and education or early intervention settings, working with children birth through age five and their families.
  • Five years of experience implementing the Pyramid Model in early childhood settings.
  • Knowledge and experience applying Implementation Science to embed evidence-based practices and research into early childhood systems and services.
  • Experience using the Pyramid Model Implementation Data System (PIDS) or similar program data management systems.
  • Experience with program evaluation, data analysis, and continuous quality improvement.
  • Experience providing coaching, training, and technical assistance to early childhood professionals and program leadership teams.
  • Experience developing and managing grants, including proposal development, evaluation planning, and grant reporting.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

  • Demonstrated ability to coordinate, develop, implement, and evaluate projects and programs from initiation through completion.
  • Knowledge of Implementation Science and its application to the adoption, implementation, and sustainability of evidence-based practices.
  • Knowledge of early childhood development, social and emotional development, and evidence-based practices for children birth through age five and their families.
  • Ability to coordinate statewide initiatives and collaborate effectively with diverse stakeholders, including state agencies, early childhood programs, and community partners.
  • Ability to collect, organize, analyze, and interpret quantitative and qualitative data and prepare reports to communicate program outcomes.
  • Knowledge of program evaluation, continuous quality improvement, and data-informed decision-making processes.
  • Ability to provide training, coaching, technical assistance, and professional development to diverse audiences.
  • Ability to make administrative and procedural decisions, establish priorities, and exercise independent judgment.
  • Strong organizational, project management, written communication, and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple projects, meet deadlines, and adapt to changing program priorities.
  • Ability to develop collaborative partnerships and facilitate group processes to support program implementation and organizational change.
  • Demonstrated ability to identify funding opportunities and contribute to grant development and sustainability planning.

College/Department Highlights

The Institute for Disability Research, Policy & Practice (IDRPP) is Utah’s federally designated University Center for Excellence in Developmental Disabilities (UCEDD). The IDRPP opened its doors in 1972 and was the first UCEDD program in the U.S. to focus on the educational and social needs of children and adults with disabilities. Over the past 50 years the IDRPP has grown into one of the largest UCEDD programs in the nation and is recognized as a pioneer in research, training, technical assistance, and services for children and adults with disabilities, their families, and the professionals who serve them.

The IDRPP is committed to hiring people with disabilities, veterans, and diverse individuals from all communities and backgrounds. We value visible and invisible differences, and we recognize that diversity makes us stronger. We welcome applicants who bring something different and unique to our organization. We value creativity, loyalty, and hard work. We believe that we can change the world and make it a better, more inclusive place for everyone, and we want to hire people who also believe that they can make a difference.

Mission

We are working together to create inclusive communities and improve the lives of children and adults with disabilities and their families through sustainable innovation, collaborative research, responsive service, and interdisciplinary training and education.

Values

  • We Innovate: We lead by developing dynamic, sustainable, forward-thinking programs and services.
  • We Include: We demonstrate how to effectively work toward inclusive communities in our planning, programs, and services. We celebrate diversity in ability, race, ethnicity, culture, language, gender, sexual orientation, politics, and religion.
  • We Collaborate: We forge partnerships. Working together makes us more effective and responsive to the current needs of our clients and communities.
  • We Care: We do what we do because we care. We are making the world a better place for people with disabilities and their families.

Funding Statement

The Institute for Disability Research, Policy, & Practice is one of the largest research and outreach centers at USU, and we are largely funded through grants, contracts, and fee-for-service programs. All staff positions at the IDRPP are contingent upon funding, and all senior staff at the IDRPP with graduate degrees are responsible for helping to generate funding to support our operations and growth.

College Highlights

The Emma Eccles Jones College of Education and Human Services is home to eight departments and is committed to providing the best learning opportunities and educational research in the state of Utah. Our programs are strengthened by an on-campus elementary laboratory school and five stand-alone centers, including the Sorenson Legacy Foundation Center for Clinical Excellence. The college offers clinical services to the community across the human lifespan and provides students with real-world service and research opportunities.

University Highlights

As Utah’s student-centered, land-grant research university, Utah State University expands opportunity and strengthens communities across the state through learning, discovery, extension, and engagement. Founded in 1888, USU now holds two Carnegie distinctions: R1 status for very high research activity and the Carnegie Community Engagement Classification. Its innovative research and scholarship is grounded in reciprocal partnerships with local, regional, and global communities, advancing knowledge and serving the public good across Utah, the nation, and the world. With over 50 world-class research facilities and the nation’s second-oldest undergraduate research program, USU prepares students to become active, civically engaged leaders who can address critical societal challenges.

USU enrolls over 29,800 students, both online and in person at locations throughout the state. Utah State’s 30 locations include a main campus in Logan, Utah, residential campuses in Price and Blanding, and six additional statewide campuses, along with education centers serving every county. USU educates students from all 50 states and more than 80 countries. For over 100 years, USU Extension has served and engaged Utahns, serving every county in the state.

Competing at the NCAA Division I level in 16 sports, USU is a proud member of the Pac-12 Conference, which it joined July 1, 2026. The Aggies capped a historic final season in the Mountain West by capturing nine combined regular-season and tournament titles in 2025-26, with five teams advancing to postseason play. This tradition of excellence extends to the classroom, where 232 student-athletes earned academic honors, and to the community, where USU ranked second nationally in Division I service hours, with nine teams placing in the top 10 for community service.

Utah State is dedicated to fostering a community where all individuals feel respected, valued, and supported and where diversity of thought and culture are cultivated. We seek to recruit, hire, and retain people from all walks of life who will champion excellence in education, research, discovery, outreach, and service. We believe that promoting a strong sense of community and belonging empowers and engages all members of USU to thrive and be successful. Forbes recognized our commitment to employees when it named Utah State the best employer in Utah in 2023. Learn more about USU.

The university provides a Dual Career Assistance Program to support careers for partners who are also seeking employment. Additionally, USU is committed to providing access and a reasonable accommodation for individuals with disabilities. To request a reasonable accommodation for a disability, contact the university’s ADA coordinator in the Office of Human Resources at 435-797-0122 or hr@usu.edu.

title: 2nd Shift Forge Operator
description:
Forge Operator

Position Purpose:

Position is responsible for forging aluminum slugs into parts using a forge press.

Essential Functions:

  • Work from production order, job ticket and/or direction of supervisor;
  • Follow work instructions to produce parts;
  • Verify the material to be forged is correct and the dimensions are according to specifications;
  • Set-up Maxi and Screw presses;
  • Set-up and remove different dies;
  • Perform checks on die and bolster plate bolts;
  • Understand press settings and troubleshoot settings when necessary;
  • Understand proper slug location, tolerances, temperature settings, tonnage, alloys and lube mixtures;
  • Identify defects/non-conforming marks in the forged parts and make appropriate corrections;
  • Complete appropriate paperwork such as visual inspection records, daily checklists, routing sign offs, etc;
  • Identify issues with the equipment and notify supervisor and/or maintenance;
  • Monitor DAS stations to ensure proper operation of press, part rate, and temperature;
  • Monitor furnace temperature and speed to ensure proper heating of slugs and/or parts;
  • Inspect dies after use and tag dies requiring further inspection or rework;
  • Notify Quality of quality issues;
  • Maintain daily timekeeping, production, and interventions on computer systems;
  • Report unusual or unsafe conditions to supervisor;
  • Actively participate in efforts to establish and promote a safe and healthy work environment. Follow policies, programs, and procedures for the reduction and elimination of work related accidents and provide feedback to promote safer work behaviors and conditions.

Education and Training:

  • High School Diploma or GED;
  • Previous experience in forging or heavy machine operation preferred.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Ability to read, comprehend, and follow instructions;
  • Ability to work under pressure and adhere to schedules;
  • Ability to read a tape measure;
  • Ability to operate hand tools such as spray gun and forge tongs;
  • Ability to work safely and keep area clean;
  • Ability to work assigned shift and remain awake and alert during assigned shift is required;
  • Reporting to work for assigned shift, maintaining a physical presence and performing assigned work for the duration of assigned shift is required;
  • Demonstrated ability to work well with all levels of the organization;
  • Good verbal, interpersonal, and written communication skills;
  • Able to communicate clearly, concisely and achieve intended objectives;
  • Ability to work in a variety of environments which may include exposure to extreme heat, humidity, fumes or airborne particles, toxic or caustic chemicals, loud noise, and all weather conditions. Reporting to work for assigned shift, maintaining a physical presence and performing assigned work for the duration of assigned shift is required;

Environmental Conditions:

  • High Temperatures: Frequently exposed to extreme heat from the forging process, necessitating proper heat-resistant gear.
  • Noise Levels: Typically works in a loud environment due to machinery and equipment, requiring the use of hearing protection.
  • Dust and Fumes: May encounter metal dust, particulates, and fumes from the forging process, making adequate ventilation essential.
  • Physical Space: Works in a potentially cramped or busy area, requiring good spatial awareness to navigate safely around machinery and other workers.
  • Safety Hazards: Regularly exposed to hazards from heavy machinery, hot materials, and moving parts, necessitating strict adherence to safety protocols.
  • Protective Equipment: Requires the use of personal protective equipment (PPE), including gloves, helmets, and flame-resistant clothing.
  • Lighting Conditions: Adequate lighting is crucial for visibility and safety, especially when handling hot or heavy materials.
  • Surface Conditions: Floors may be uneven or slippery due to oils and water, requiring caution and proper footwear.
  • Physical Stamina: The job often involves physical labor, such as lifting and moving heavy objects, requiring good physical fitness.
  • Team Environment: Works closely with other team members, necessitating effective communication and teamwork in a potentially chaotic setting.

Physical Demands:

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to talk and hear. The employee is regularly required to use hands to finger, handle, or feel and reach with hands and arms. The employee is regularly required to stand for an 8 hour shift. Position requires frequent twisting, turning, reaching, bending, pulling and pushing. Position occasionally requires walking, climbing, stooping, and crouching. The employee must be able to handle up to 80 lbs on a regular basis throughout the 8 hour shift. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision. Working conditions include exposure to extreme temperatures (heat) and humid conditions, dirt, and noise

Behavioral Traits:

  • Attention to Detail: Precision is critical in forging. Operators must be meticulous about measurements, temperatures, and timings.
  • Safety Awareness: Given the hazards associated with hot metals and heavy machinery, a strong commitment to safety protocols is essential.
  • Problem-Solving Skills: The ability to troubleshoot issues that arise during the forging process is vital, whether it's equipment malfunction or material inconsistencies.
  • Technical Aptitude: A solid understanding of machinery, metallurgy, and the forging process helps operators work efficiently and make informed decisions.
  • Physical Stamina: The job often requires standing for long periods, lifting heavy materials, and performing repetitive tasks.
  • Team Collaboration: Forge operators often work as part of a team, so good communication and collaboration skills are important.
  • Adaptability: The ability to adjust to new processes, tools, or changes in production requirements is crucial in a dynamic manufacturing environment.
  • Time Management: Meeting production deadlines requires effective prioritization and time management skills.
  • Initiative: Proactively identifying areas for improvement in processes or equipment can lead to better efficiency and quality.
  • Focus: Maintaining concentration for extended periods helps ensure quality and prevents accidents.

Pay & Benefits

Rate: In accordance with applicable pay transparency laws, the hourly payrate for this position is $19 - $29 USD. This payrate is provided to ensure transparency and compliance with local, state, and federal regulations.

title: Assistant Manager
description:
Being in charge comes with great responsibility. You are responsible for everything that happens during your shift. This includes all cost controls, inventory control, cash control and customer relations. You are the leader – so set the example! You must follow ALL policies and procedures 100% of the time and expect the same from your crew. Additionally, you have the opportunity to lead a team toward a common, outstanding goal: sell more pizzas, have more fun! In doing so, you will be responsible for staffing, paperwork submission, food management, scheduling, maintaining image standards, store cleanliness, marketing, and profitability. Additional requirements and responsibilities include, but are not limited to the following:

  • Ability to direct activities, perform repetitive tasks, work alone and with others, work under stress, meet strict quality control standards, coordinate with coworkers and customers, analyze and compile data, make sound, ethical judgments and decisions in a timely manner.
  • Enthusiastic customer greeting and positive personality – taking orders and fielding customer concerns with a smile!
  • Operate, clean, and maintain all store facility and equipment.

  • Establish positive working relationships with end users through patience, active listening, and effective communication.
  • Assess, prioritize, and manage support requests based on urgency, business impact, and established service expectations.
  • Escalate unresolved or complex technical issues to the appropriate IT personnel or third-party support providers.
  • Record, track, and maintain accurate documentation of support requests, troubleshooting steps, decisions, and resolutions through final completion.
  • Utilize diagnostic tools and troubleshooting techniques to identify and resolve hardware, software, network, and system-related issues.
  • Research and utilize software updates, drivers, technical documentation, knowledge bases, and other resources to support problem resolution.
  • Identify recurring technical issues and recommend improvements to reduce future support requests.
  1. Desktop, Hardware, and Software Support
  • Install, configure, maintain, and upgrade computer hardware, software, peripherals, and related equipment.
  • Provide hands-on technical support for desktop computers, laptops, printers, mobile devices, and other workplace technology.
  • Configure operating systems, applications, user accounts, and system settings in accordance with organizational standards.
  • Assist with file backups, system configurations, and other routine technology maintenance activities.
  • Perform preventative maintenance, including inspecting and cleaning workstations, printers, and peripheral equipment.
  • Ensure supported hardware and software are functioning properly and meet established organizational standards.
  • Test and verify technical solutions to ensure issues have been properly resolved.
  • Follow up with end users after issue resolution to confirm satisfaction and ensure continued system functionality.
  • Develop and maintain user guides, help sheets, frequently asked questions, and other technical support documentation.
  • Maintain awareness of supported hardware, software, applications, and technology standards used throughout the organization.
  1. Network Support and Administration
  • Provide first-level support for network connectivity issues, including wired and wireless connections, VPN access, and internet connectivity.
  • Assist with troubleshooting network-related issues involving computers, printers, servers, and other connected devices.
  • Support the setup, configuration, and maintenance of network-connected devices and equipment in accordance with established IT procedures.
  • Assist with identifying and resolving connectivity issues, network access problems, and basic configuration issues.
  • Support network access for employees, including troubleshooting connectivity and authentication issues.
  • Assist with monitoring and reporting network performance issues, outages, and unusual activity to the appropriate IT personnel.
  • Maintain accurate documentation of network-related support requests, troubleshooting activities, and resolutions.
  • Escalate complex network issues, infrastructure concerns, and potential vulnerabilities to the appropriate IT personnel or service providers.
  1. Cybersecurity and Information Security Support
  • Assist in maintaining the security and integrity of company computers, systems, networks, and information.
  • Help maintain endpoint security by ensuring computers and supported devices have current antivirus, anti-malware, operating system, and security updates.
  • Assist with routine system updates, security patching, and basic security compliance activities.
  • Support user account administration, including account setup, password resets, access permissions, and account deactivation as authorized.
  • Assist with implementing and maintaining multifactor authentication (MFA) and other established security controls.
  • Monitor and report potential security concerns, suspicious activity, unusual system behavior, and possible cybersecurity incidents to the appropriate IT personnel.
  • Assist with identifying and responding to phishing emails, suspicious links, malware alerts, and other potential security threats.
  • Assist with maintaining compliance with organizational IT security policies, procedures, and acceptable-use standards.
  • Follow established procedures for data backups, recovery support, and protection of company information.
  • Assist with maintaining accurate records of IT assets, hardware configurations, software installations, and assigned equipment.
  • Promptly escalate suspected security incidents, unauthorized access, malware infections, and other significant security risks.
  • Maintain confidentiality and safeguard company systems, networks, and information in accordance with organizational security policies and procedures.
  1. Customer Service and User Support
  • Deliver responsive, professional, and customer-focused technical assistance to employees throughout the organization.
  • Explain technical issues and solutions in clear, user-friendly language appropriate to the end user's level of technical knowledge.
  • Demonstrate patience, professionalism, and a service-oriented approach when assisting employees with technical challenges.
  • Maintain effective communication with users regarding the status of open support requests and anticipated resolutions.
  • Identify opportunities to improve the end-user technology experience and overall support processes.
  1. Departmental Collaboration and Other Responsibilities
  • Collaborate with IT team members, management, and other departments to resolve technical issues and support business needs.
  • Assist with technology-related projects, system implementations, upgrades, and process improvements as assigned.
  • Perform additional duties and special projects as assigned.

title: Domino's Closing Shift Delivery Expert
description:
Domino's is seeking a reliable and customer-focused Closing Shift Delivery Expert to join our team in Kaysville, Utah. In this role, you'll be the face of Domino's, delivering hot, fresh pizzas and other menu items directly to our valued customers. We're looking for someone who takes pride in providing exceptional service while maintaining efficient delivery times. Your dedication to customer satisfaction and safe driving practices will be essential to our success.

  • Deliver pizzas and food orders to customers in a timely and professional manner
  • Maintain a clean and well-organized delivery vehicle
  • Operate GPS and run Domino's delivery management systems to plan efficient routes
  • Handle cash and card transactions accurately and securely
  • Provide friendly and courteous customer service at each delivery point
  • Ensure orders are complete and accurate before leaving the store
  • Communicate effectively with store staff regarding delivery status and customer feedback
  • Follow all traffic laws and safety regulations while operating a vehicle
  • Respond professionally to customer inquiries and resolve delivery-related issues
  • Maintain a positive attitude and represent Domino's brand values in all customer interactions
  • Daily/Nightly in-store duties will include but not limited to answering phones, oven work, washing dishes, sweeping and mopping floors, teamwork, handling food, food prep, and training.
  • Valid driver's license with a clean driving record
  • Reliable vehicle with current and proper insurance and registration
  • Proficiency with GPS navigation and delivery tracking systems
  • Strong time management and organizational skills
  • Excellent customer service and communication abilities
  • Ability to handle cash transactions and maintain accuracy
  • Physical capability to carry and deliver food orders safely
  • Familiarity with the Kaysville area (preferred)
  • Previous delivery or customer service experience (preferred)
  • Problem-solving skills and ability to handle challenging situations professionally
  • Ability to work independently and meet delivery time expectations

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS, including, but not limited to the following:

Standing

Most tasks are performed from a standing position. Walking surfaces include ceramic tile "bricks" with linoleum in some food process areas. Height of work surfaces is between 36" and 48".

Walking

For short distances for short durations

Delivery personnel must travel between the store and delivery vehicle and from the delivery vehicle to the customer's location.

Standing

A lot of your scheduled time outside of your delivery vehicle will be in-store standing for various lengths of time.

Lifting

Bulk product deliveries are made three times a week and are unloaded by the team member.

Deliveries may include cases of ingredients and supplies weighing up to 50 pounds with dimensions of up to 3' x 1.5'.

Cases are usually lifted from floor and stacked onto shelves up to 72" high.

Carrying

Large boxes, weighing 5+ pounds, are carried from the delivery carts to storage shelves.

Occasionally, pizza sauce weighing 30 pounds is carried from the storage room to the front of the store.

Trays of pizza dough are carried two at a time over short distances, and weigh approximately 3 pounds per tray.

During delivery, carry pizzas and beverages while performing "walking" and "climbing" duties.

Pushing

To move trays which are placed on dollies.

A stack of trays on a dolly is approximately 24" - 30" and requires a force of up to 7.5 pounds to push.

Trays may also be pulled.

Climbing

Team members must infrequently navigate stairs or climb a ladder to wash signs, wash walls/windows, perform maintenance.

During delivery of product, navigation of five or more flights of stairs may be required.

Stooping/Bending

Forward bending at the waist is necessary at the pizza assembly station.

Duration of this position is approximately 30 - 45 seconds at one time, repeated continuously during the day.

Forward bending is also present at the front counter and when stocking ingredients.

Crouching/Squatting

Performed occasionally to stock shelves and to clean low areas.

Reaching

Reaching is performed continuously; up, down and forward.

Workers reach above 72" occasionally to turn on/off oven controls, change prices on sign, and lift and lower objects to and from shelves.

Workers reaching down to perform such tasks as scooping cornmeal from a plastic barrel, or washing dishes.

Workers reach forward when obtaining topping ingredients, cleaning work surfaces, or answering phones.

Driving

Deliver pizzas within a designated delivery area. A Team Member may make several deliveries per shift.

Machines, Tools, Equipment, Work Aids

Team Members may be required to utilize pencils/pens, computers, telephones, calculators, TDD equipment, pizza cutter and pizza peel.

Driving Specific Job Duties

Deliver product by car and then to door of customer.

Deliver flyers and door hangers.

Requires

Valid driver's license with safe driving record meeting company standards.

Access to properly insured vehicle which can be used for delivery.

title: Cable and Optics Engineer
description:
Infrastructure Solutions Group (ISG) builds the products that power infrastructure, solutions, and data management our customers need most. Our teams design and develop the hardware and software that connect infrastructure, accelerate computational workloads, integrate across the stack, protect data continuity, and deliver the platforms, applications, and diagnostics our customers rely on every day at enterprise scale.

Some product builders follow the rules. Ours rewrite them.

Within ISG, innovation isn't just about creating new technology- it's about challenging assumptions and reimagining how work gets done. Engineers define intent, author precise specifications, and orchestrate AI agents that execute at speed and scale. AI is embedded throughout our development process, helping us move faster, learn quicker, and deliver greater impact. Yet the most important contribution remains uniquely human: deciding what to build, designing how it should work, and applying the judgment needed to earn our customers' trust. When your products power critical infrastructure around the world, that responsibility matters.

We move quickly toward the work that matters most. We reward experimentation, encourage bold thinking, and remove unnecessary barriers so great ideas can become reality faster. Our teams embrace a customer-first, first-to-market mindset, transforming rapid feedback into better products and better outcomes. We aren't looking for people who are content with the status quo- we look for builders who question it, improve it, and occasionally rewrite it.

If you're energized by solving complex systems challenges, excited to work alongside AI to amplify your impact, and motivated by the opportunity to shape what's next instead of simply maintaining what's been done before, you'll find your place here.

Electrical Senior Engineer – Cables & Optics

Join us as a Electrical Senior Engineer on our Cables & Optics team in Santa Clara, CA to do the best work of your career and make a profound social impact.

What you’ll achieve

As a member of the Network Hardware Engineering team, you will be responsible for the verification and qualification of server, storage, and network hardware, including NICs, switches, copper cables, and optical transceiver modules, primarily in the 10 Gbit/s to 1600 Gbit/s range. This role involves validating the performance, interoperability, and reliability of hardware and connectivity solutions and supporting their integration into Dell products. You will collaborate with cross-functional teams, including Platform Engineering, Solutions Engineering, COMMs, Network Software, and Product Management, on matters related to datacenter and GenAI-focused network, compute, storage, and switch platforms. As an Electrical Senior Engineer, you will help ensure the successful deployment of high-speed server, storage, and network technologies across Dell's next-generation infrastructure portfolio.

You will:

  • Develop and execute test plans to verify and qualify server, storage, and network hardware, including cables and optical modules, across a wide range of speeds and protocols

  • Perform hands-on laboratory validation, interoperability testing, performance characterization, and failure analysis of server, storage, and network hardware; analyze test results and drive issue resolution with internal teams and suppliers

  • Collaborate with platform, networking, firmware, and software engineering teams to ensure successful integration and deployment of hardware components within compute, storage, and networking products

  • Work with server, storage, network, cable, optical module, NIC, switch, and silicon vendors to evaluate product capabilities, review technical specifications, and support qualification, production readiness, and sustaining activities

  • Ensure qualified hardware solutions meet system requirements for performance, reliability, manufacturability, and serviceability while supporting new product introductions and sustaining programs

Take the first step towards your dream career

Every Dell Technologies team member brings something unique to the table. Here’s what we are looking for with this role:

Essential Requirements

    • 3+ years of experience in hardware validation, qualification, or testing of server, storage, or network hardware, including high-speed networking, optical transceivers, and cable technologies

    • Familiarity with server, storage, and network hardware platforms and their interconnects, such as NICs, switches, PCIe, and optical and copper solutions (e.g., SFP+, QSFP+, QSFP28, QSFP-DD, OSFP, DAC, AOC)

    • Experience developing and executing test plans and performing hands-on laboratory validation, interoperability testing, and troubleshooting of server, storage, and network hardware, including server-to-switch and switch-to-switch connectivity

    • Working knowledge of Ethernet networking concepts and experience using common lab equipment and test tools for server, storage, and network hardware

    • Strong analytical, problem-solving, communication, and documentation skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively with cross-functional engineering teams and external suppliers

Desirable Requirements

    • BS in Electrical Engineering or a related field; MS preferred

    • Familiarity with data center server, storage, and networking technologies and key industry suppliers of servers, storage systems, switches, NICs, optical transceivers, and cables

    • Experience with Broadcom-based networking platforms and SDKs, Ethernet and InfiniBand technologies, or AI/HPC networking environments is a plus

Compensation

Dell is committed to fair and equitable compensation practices. The salary range for this position is $133k - $173k.

title: Cables & Optics Engineer
description:
Our Electrical Engineering team puts the spark into the full hardware development lifecycle, from concept to production. It takes experts in system architecture definition, design, analysis, prototyping, sourcing & the debugging and validation of layouts or routes to deliver state-of-the-art products for a changing world. We work closely with designers, cross-functional teams within Dell Technologies and suppliers to make sure electronic designs meet a range of requirements, including schedule, feature set, functionality and quality, as well as industry standards.

Join us to do the best work of your career and make a profound social impact as an Electrical Engineer 2 on our Networking Hardware Engineering Team in Taipei, Taiwan.

What you’ll achieve

As a member of the Networking HW Engineering team, the Cables & Optics Engineer will be responsible for the verification and qualification of complex copper cables and optical fiber transceiver modules in various systems, primarily in the 10 Gbit/s – 1600 Gbit/s range. This role requires collaboration with functional HW & SW Engineering team, including Platform, Solution, COMMs, Network SW, etc., on all matters related to datacenter and GenAI-focused network compute, storage, and switch connectivity using optical and copper technologies.

  • Designs, develops, modifies, and evaluates electronic parts, components, or integrated circuitry for electronic equipment and other hardware systems.

  • Analyzes equipment and test plan requirements to perform verification; conducts experimental tests and evaluates results.

  • Work with lead engineer or architect to select components based on analysis of specifications, cost, continuity of supply, and reliability.

  • Reviews original design manufacturer and sub-tier vendor capability to support product development and production.

  • Ensures the manufacturability, reliability, and serviceability of designs, and designs integrate with the rest of product functions including mechanical and software.

  • 4+ years of related experience in a professional role with a Bachelor’s degree; or 2+ years with a Master’s degree of experience in Fiber Optic Communication and HW Product Development and Validation

  • Solid understanding of high-speed pluggable transceiver form-factors and MSAs, SFP+/QSFP+/QSFP-DD/OSFP connectors, cages and their mechanical and thermal design.

  • Have a good understanding with electrical simulation tools, understanding of the different tools available for simulation.

  • Highly self-motivated with a strong multi-disciplinary background.

title: Project Manager
description:
· Bachelor’s degree in Business, Information Systems, Project Management, or related field (or equivalent experience).

· 5+ years of project management experience delivering cross-functional projects.

· Proven track record of delivering projects on scope, on schedule, and within budget.

· Strong leadership, facilitation, and communication skills, with the ability to work effectively with stakeholders at all levels.

· Working knowledge of project management methodologies (Agile, Waterfall, Hybrid).

· Proficiency in PM tools (e.g., MS Project, Jira, Smartsheet).

· Experience delivering technology, data, or enterprise software.

· PMP, CAPM, or equivalent certification preferred.

RESPONSIBILITIES – HOW THIS POSITION SUPPORTS THE VISION include the following, but are not limited to:

· Lead assigned projects from planning through implementation, helping ensure they are delivered successfully against agreed scope, schedule, and objectives.

· Develop and maintain project plans, timelines, milestones, and dependencies.

· Manage timelines, identify and mitigate risks, resolve issues, and escalate to the Director of the PMO and project sponsors when needed.

· Drive decisions by framing options, facilitating discussion, and securing timely approvals from sponsors and stakeholders.

· Identify resource requirements for each project and source the resources needed across the business, IT, and vendors.

· Manage scope and change control, and track project budgets and spend against approved amounts.

· Provide clear, consistent status reporting to sponsors, stakeholders, and PMO leadership.

· Drive follow-up on key actions and decisions, and assemble stakeholders for meetings and workshops.

· Follow PMO governance, methodology, and templates, and contribute ideas to improve them.

· Support change management and adoption so that delivered projects achieve their intended business outcomes.

· Capture lessons learned at project close and share them with the PMO team.

INDICATORS OF PERFORMANCE

· On-Time Delivery Rate: Percentage of assigned projects completed on or before the agreed timeline (Target: ≥ 80%).

· Budget Adherence: Percentage of assigned projects delivered within approved budget (Target: ≥ 90%).

· Scope Control: Percentage of scope changes formally approved before work begins (Target: 100%).

· Process Compliance Rate: Percentage of assigned projects following PMO standards and governance (Target: ≥ 90%).

· Communication Effectiveness: Timeliness and clarity of project reporting (Target: ≥ 95% of reports delivered on schedule).

· Risk Mitigation Success: Percentage of identified risks successfully mitigated (Target: ≥ 90%).

· Training & Development: Completion of professional development goals (Target: 100%).

title: Domino's Closing Shift Delivery Expert
description:
Domino's is seeking a reliable and customer-focused Closing Shift Delivery Expert to join our team in Woods Cross, Utah. In this role, you'll be the face of Domino's, delivering hot, fresh pizzas and other menu items directly to our valued customers. We're looking for someone who takes pride in providing exceptional service while maintaining efficient delivery times. Your dedication to customer satisfaction and safe driving practices will be essential to our success.

  • Deliver pizzas and food orders to customers in a timely and professional manner
  • Maintain a clean and well-organized delivery vehicle
  • Operate GPS and run Domino's delivery management systems to plan efficient routes
  • Handle cash and card transactions accurately and securely
  • Provide friendly and courteous customer service at each delivery point
  • Ensure orders are complete and accurate before leaving the store
  • Communicate effectively with store staff regarding delivery status and customer feedback
  • Follow all traffic laws and safety regulations while operating a vehicle
  • Respond professionally to customer inquiries and resolve delivery-related issues
  • Maintain a positive attitude and represent Domino's brand values in all customer interactions
  • Daily/Nightly in-store duties will include but not limited to answering phones, oven work, washing dishes, sweeping and mopping floors, teamwork, handling food, food prep, and training.
  • Valid driver's license with a clean driving record
  • Reliable vehicle with current and proper insurance and registration
  • Proficiency with GPS navigation and delivery tracking systems
  • Strong time management and organizational skills
  • Excellent customer service and communication abilities
  • Ability to handle cash transactions and maintain accuracy
  • Physical capability to carry and deliver food orders safely
  • Familiarity with the Bountiful and Woods Cross area (preferred)
  • Previous delivery or customer service experience (preferred)
  • Problem-solving skills and ability to handle challenging situations professionally
  • Ability to work independently and meet delivery time expectations

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS, including, but not limited to the following:

Standing

Most tasks are performed from a standing position. Walking surfaces include ceramic tile "bricks" with linoleum in some food process areas. Height of work surfaces is between 36" and 48".

Walking

For short distances for short durations

Delivery personnel must travel between the store and delivery vehicle and from the delivery vehicle to the customer's location.

Standing

A lot of your scheduled time outside of your delivery vehicle will be in-store standing for various lengths of time.

Lifting

Bulk product deliveries are made three times a week and are unloaded by the team member.

Deliveries may include cases of ingredients and supplies weighing up to 50 pounds with dimensions of up to 3' x 1.5'.

Cases are usually lifted from floor and stacked onto shelves up to 72" high.

Carrying

Large boxes, weighing 5+ pounds, are carried from the delivery carts to storage shelves.

Occasionally, pizza sauce weighing 30 pounds is carried from the storage room to the front of the store.

Trays of pizza dough are carried two at a time over short distances, and weigh approximately 3 pounds per tray.

During delivery, carry pizzas and beverages while performing "walking" and "climbing" duties.

Pushing

To move trays which are placed on dollies.

A stack of trays on a dolly is approximately 24" - 30" and requires a force of up to 7.5 pounds to push.

Trays may also be pulled.

Climbing

Team members must infrequently navigate stairs or climb a ladder to wash signs, wash walls/windows, perform maintenance.

During delivery of product, navigation of five or more flights of stairs may be required.

Stooping/Bending

Forward bending at the waist is necessary at the pizza assembly station.

Duration of this position is approximately 30 - 45 seconds at one time, repeated continuously during the day.

Forward bending is also present at the front counter and when stocking ingredients.

Crouching/Squatting

Performed occasionally to stock shelves and to clean low areas.

Reaching

Reaching is performed continuously; up, down and forward.

Workers reach above 72" occasionally to turn on/off oven controls, change prices on sign, and lift and lower objects to and from shelves.

Workers reaching down to perform such tasks as scooping cornmeal from a plastic barrel, or washing dishes.

Workers reach forward when obtaining topping ingredients, cleaning work surfaces, or answering phones.

Driving

Deliver pizzas within a designated delivery area. A Team Member may make several deliveries per shift.

Machines, Tools, Equipment, Work Aids

Team Members may be required to utilize pencils/pens, computers, telephones, calculators, TDD equipment, pizza cutter and pizza peel.

Driving Specific Job Duties

Deliver product by car and then to door of customer.

Deliver flyers and door hangers.

Requires

Valid driver's license with safe driving record meeting company standards.

Access to a properly insured vehicle which can be used for delivery.

  • Conhecimento em gestão de ativos de TI, telefonia corporativa e suporte a sistemas de gestão empresarial (ERP) e de relacionamento com clientes (CRM).
  • Facilidade para dialogar com equipes técnicas, fornecedores e áreas de negócio e traduzir questões técnicas em orientações claras.

title: Senior Product Management – Team Lead, Core+ Launch
description:
Senior Consultant, Product Management

Showcasing excellence and innovation at every stage, Product Management is responsible for the cross-functional management of products or solutions through their entire lifecycle. Using a wealth of technical and industry experience, we work across functional areas to implement our products or solutions. We undertake thorough analysis of the markets to ensure we maximize profitability and adjust our product strategies to respond to competition. Our role also involves acting as subject matter experts for internal and external product events or partner meetings.

What you’ll achieve:

As a Senior Consultant, you will serve as a principal individual contributor shaping complex product strategies. You will lead market research, pricing/packaging, and roadmap narratives for executive decisions. You will influence cross-functional leaders with compelling analyses and measurable results.

In this Team Lead role, you will lead the Core+ Launch Product Management team in Round Rock, Texas, owning the strategy, processes, and execution that take Core+ products and solutions from definition to ready-to-ship (RTS) and into the market. You will coach and develop a team of launch product managers and partner closely with Product Group, Engineering, Global Operations, Supply Chain, Sales, Services, and Marketing to drive cross-functional readiness, keeping customer requirements at the center of every launch. You will also set the launch operating rhythm and present launch status, risks, and recommendations to the VP of Core+ Product Management and senior leadership.

Join us to do the best work of your career and make a profound social impact as a Senior Consultant on our Product Management team.

You will:

  • Lead, coach, and develop a team of launch product managers, setting clear priorities and balancing launch portfolios by business priority, complexity, and risk
  • Own the end-to-end Core+ launch process from product definition through RTS, general availability, and post-launch review, including the integrated launch calendar, launch gates, success criteria, and KPIs
  • Drive cross-functional launch readiness across SKU and BOM enablement, pricing, configurator and quoting tools, supply positioning, services, and sales enablement
  • Partner with Sales and customer-facing teams to ensure launch plans reflect customer requirements, market timing, and competitive positioning, and use post-launch feedback to improve future launches and the product roadmap
  • Influence Director, VP, and executive leaders with clear narratives on launch risks, tradeoffs, and resource needs, while simplifying and standardizing launch processes with AI and automation

Take the first step towards your dream career

Every Dell Technologies team member brings something unique to the table. Here’s what we are looking for with this role:

Essential Requirements

  • 15+ years of related experience, including product management, product launch, or new product introduction (NPI) for enterprise hardware or solutions
  • Proven experience leading teams, with people management or formal team lead responsibilities
  • Deep understanding of the end-to-end product lifecycle and launch readiness, including SKU/BOM, pricing, supply chain, services, and sales enablement
  • Advanced craft across research, strategy, and analytics, with fluency in experimentation and product metrics
  • Demonstrated impact via experiments, metrics, and outcomes, including leading complex, cross-functional programs with many dependencies and fast timelines
  • Strong storytelling and influence skills, including presenting to VP and C-suite stakeholders and influencing without direct authority

Desirable Requirements

  • Master's degree or MBA (e.g., Business/Analytics, Engineering, Computer Science, or related field) or relevant certifications (e.g., Pragmatic Institute PMC, AIPMM CPM, SAFe PO/PM)
  • Experience with server, storage, networking, AI infrastructure, or rack-scale solutions, and in designing or modernizing launch or NPI processes using AI tools

Our Electrical Engineering team puts the spark into the full hardware development lifecycle, from concept to production. It takes experts in system architecture definition, design, analysis, prototyping, sourcing & the debugging and validation of layouts or routes to deliver state-of-the-art products for a changing world. We work closely with designers, cross-functional teams within Dell Technologies and suppliers to make sure electronic designs meet a range of requirements, including schedule, feature set, functionality and quality, as well as industry standards.

Join us to do the best work of your career and make a profound social impact as a Electrical Principal Engineer on our Component Engineering Team in Taiwan.

  • Ensure NPU, CPU, PHY, Memory, SSD,ICs, electrical cables/connectors selected meet manufacturability, reliability and testability goals. Leverage/manage production tools to standardize and specify the NPU, CPU, PHY, Memory, SSD,ICs, electrical cables/connectors for BOM implementation.

SUMMARY: Abrades surfaces of parts by sand blasting to remove adhering scale, paint, grease, tar, rust and dirt. Operates cone, disk, or nozzle type electrostatic painting equipment within designated paint booths. Required to perform other miscellaneous tasks as supervision deems necessary.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES include the following. Other duties may be assigned.

· Shovels or pours abrasives such as sand, grit, or shot of specified grade into machine hopper.

· Masks specified areas of object to protect from abrading action.

· Loads parts on racks in enclosed rooms, into tumbling barrels, or into cabinets.

· Regulates pressure and composition of abrasive mixture flowing through nozzle or into tumbling barrel.

· Starts equipment that directs blast or flow of abrasive laden compressed air, gas, or liquid over surface of parts.

· Directs nozzle over surface of large parts or inserts arms through glove fitted cabinet openings and manipulates small parts under nozzle for specified interval.

· Examines finished parts to ensure conformance to specifications.

· Adjusts valves and observes gauges to set pressure and to control flow of paint to each spray station.

· Inspects painted units for runs, sags, and unpainted areas.

· Readjusts pressure valves to control direction and pattern of spray and to correct flaws in coating.

· Cleans paint from ceiling and walls of booth, conveyor hooks or grid, and from disks, cones, spray heads, and hoses.

· Hand sprays parts to cover unpainted areas or apply rust preventative.

· Mixes paint according to specifications with viscometer to regulate consistency.
